Note::squeeze¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::squeeze(std::int64_t dim) const

Drop A Size-1 Axis¶

squeeze(dim) removes axis dim if its size is 1, lowering the rank by one. Use it to undo an unsqueeze, to peel a leading batch axis of length 1 back off a result, or to turn a 1 × n / n × 1 shape into a plain n.

Nothing about the text changes: cells are shared with the source, the bytes-vs-UTF-8 mode carries over, and only the shape metadata is rewritten.

The dim contract¶

  • dim counts from the front (0) or, when negative, from the back (-1 is the last axis). After that wrap it must land in [0, dim()), otherwise the call raises dim out of range.

  • If axis dim is not size 1, the Note is returned unchanged — this is not an error. squeeze only ever removes a length-1 axis.

  • On a 0-D Note there is no axis to address and the Note is returned unchanged.

This method never removes more than one axis and takes no “squeeze every size-1 axis” form; call it once per axis you want gone.

Example 1: Drop A Leading 1¶

const auto row = pluss::make_note({{"x", "y", "z"}});   // shape [1, 3]
std::cout << pluss::note::print(row.squeeze(0)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["x", "y", "z"]

Example 2: Drop A Trailing 1¶

const auto col = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"}).reshape({6, 1});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(col.squeeze(1)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"]

Example 3: A Negative Axis¶

const auto row = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"}).reshape({1, 6});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(row.squeeze(-2)) << "\n";   // -2 is axis 0

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"]

Example 4: The Axis Is Not Size 1 — No Change¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.squeeze(0)) << "\n";      // axis 0 has size 2

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::make_note("solo").squeeze(0)) << "\n";  // scalar

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b", "c"], 
  ["d", "e", "f"]
]
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"solo"

See Also¶

  • Note::unsqueeze: the inverse — insert a size-1 axis.

  • Note::reshape: restate the whole shape when more than one axis changes.

  • Note::flatten: collapse every axis, not just a size-1 one.
